::: {#exm-irls-six-patients}

#### IRLS on the six-patient trial

The code runs [IRLS](#def-irls) from $\vcoef^* = \vzero$ on the data of the [six-patient trial](#exm-logistic-regression)
and compares the result with the coefficients from `glm()`.

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# design matrix: intercept and group (-1 control, +1 treatment); y = 1 means recovered
irls_x <- cbind(1, rep(c(-1, 1), each = 3))
irls_y <- c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1)
# start from zero coefficients and take six IRLS steps
irls_coef <- c(0, 0)
irls_path <- data.frame(step = 0, intercept = 0, slope = 0)
for (step in 1:6) {
  prob <- plogis(drop(irls_x %*% irls_coef))
  weight <- prob * (1 - prob)
  work_resp <- drop(irls_x %*% irls_coef) + (irls_y - prob) / weight
  irls_coef <- drop(solve(crossprod(irls_x, weight * irls_x),
                          crossprod(irls_x, weight * work_resp)))
  irls_path[step + 1, ] <- c(step, irls_coef)
}
irls_path
# the maximum likelihood fit from glm()
coef(glm(irls_y ~ irls_x[, 2], family = binomial))
```

The first step moves the slope to $`r round(irls_path$slope[2], 4)`$, which is $2/3$ ([the hand computation](#exr-irls-step)).
After six steps the slope is $`r round(irls_path$slope[7], 6)`$,
and it differs from the `glm()` slope by `r format(abs(irls_path$slope[7] - coef(glm(irls_y ~ irls_x[, 2], family = binomial))[[2]]), digits = 2)`.
The slope settles at $\log 2 = `r round(log(2), 6)`$,
the log odds ratio between the treatment group (recovery odds $2$) and the control group (recovery odds $1/2$) divided by $2$, since the groups are coded $\pm 1$.

:::
